input: Source a secondhand sewing machine for alterations

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A strict budget ceiling rules out certain machines, sellers, and platforms entirely — it is the single biggest filter on options.
The type of alterations (e.g. hemming lightweight fabrics vs. heavy denim or leather) determines the mechanical specs and features the machine must have.
Whether this is for personal occasional use or semi-professional/high-volume work changes the required durability and feature set dramatically.
Preferred sourcing location (local pick-up, online shipping, specific platforms) affects logistics, ability to test before buying, and risk tolerance.
Brand loyalty or aversion, mechanical vs. computerised preference, or familiarity with certain models shapes which options to prioritise.
Knowing what 'good condition' means to the user — tested and serviced, cosmetic wear acceptable, age limits — sets the quality bar for evaluating listings.
The user's sewing experience level determines whether setup guidance, a simpler machine, or a service/tune-up on purchase needs to be part of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Source a secondhand sewing machine for alterations
gold.taskDescription: Find and acquire a used sewing machine suited for doing clothing alterations.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for this machine?
questions.description: Establish a hard spending ceiling to filter platforms, machine brands, and age ranges from the start.

questions.title: What kinds of alterations will you mainly use it for?
questions.description: Identify the fabric types and tasks (e.g. hemming trousers, taking in seams, heavy canvas) to define the minimum mechanical requirements.

questions.title: Is this for personal use or higher-volume work?
questions.description: Determine whether light home use or frequent/semi-professional output is expected, which affects the durability and duty-cycle needed.

questions.title: Do you want to buy locally or are you open to online sellers?
questions.description: Decide whether local pick-up and in-person testing is a priority, or if online platforms with shipping are acceptable.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred brand or machine type in mind?
questions.description: Capture any brand preferences, past experience with specific models, or mechanical-vs-computerised requirements to narrow the shortlist.

questions.title: What condition standard must the machine meet to be acceptable?
questions.description: Define the user's quality bar — e.g. recently serviced, fully tested, cosmetic wear tolerated, age limits — so listings can be evaluated consistently.

questions.title: How experienced are you with using a sewing machine?
questions.description: Gauge the user's skill level to determine whether ease of setup, simplified controls, or a service check on purchase should be factored into the plan.
